claims.claim: Current deterministic Agent X-Change experiment fixtures satisfy the repository's encoded checks for their frozen cases.
claims.oracle: Repository-controlled fixtures, smoke tests, and scorers
claims.falsifier: A maintained frozen fixture fails its stated deterministic check or provenance is incomplete.
limitations: Cold/model isolation does not create independent external authority or general protocol superiority.

claims.claim: For the four frozen Experiment 002 relation-tuple tasks, an RFC 8259 JSON-array encoding using the same numeric relation IDs and ordered arguments round-trips the same tuples and is 1 UTF-8 byte smaller per compact packet than the equivalent whitespace-minimized Agent X-Change text form.
claims.status: 4/4 semantic tuple round trips; JSON 132 bytes vs compact AX 136 bytes total
claims.oracle: RFC 8259 JSON syntax plus frozen evidence baseline schema evidence/external/baselines/json-array-v1.json
claims.falsifier: Any frozen task fails exact tuple round-trip equivalence, or a byte recount under the stated encodings differs from the recorded result.
limitations: Comparison uses the same shared numeric relation vocabulary and ordered arguments in both encodings.
The JSON packet schema is explicitly frozen by this campaign; RFC 8259 specifies JSON syntax, not Agent X-Change semantics.
Compact Agent X-Change strings are equivalent whitespace-minimized forms for this frozen experiment subset and are not declared canonical IsoGraph serialization.
No parser-speed, general protocol superiority, compression, binary encoding, or schema-discovery-cost claim is made.

claims.claim: Agent X-Change has general semantic, efficiency, or security superiority over external protocol or serialization baselines.
claims.falsifier: Comparable baseline tests fail to show the claimed property or reveal semantic/authority loss.
limitations: The first fair JSON-array byte baseline is unfavorable to Agent X-Change by 1 byte per frozen task; broader objectives require separate task-appropriate baselines.
